source.title: Recruited and Erased: Head-Level Provenance of Safety Detection in Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether selected harm-detection heads are needed for refusal and argues that detection and refusal execution are separable, refining the direction-level account.
record.gate_note: The paper uses community-released abliterated checkpoints and measures their detection scores; it states that weight-level abliteration breaks refusal outright. It does not itself extract and ablate/add the original difference-in-means residual direction at every layer and position. It also does not test attacks suppressing that direction or training against its ablation. Results cited from other work are not cataloged.
record.test_reason: The paper argues that the single-direction account conflates harm detection with refusal execution. It tests this by zero-ablating head sets selected for harm detection and finding refusal unchanged, and by reading harm detection with a probe after community abliteration. These are its own results on V5 (harm encoded separately from refusal). It does not extract, ablate or add the difference-in-means direction itself (V1). It also gives no measured refusal rates for the abliterated checkpoints, which it uses as a tool (V2).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that safety fine-tuning recruits, rather than builds, harm-detection heads from a pretrained substrate whose base separation is bounded by input text. Abliteration erases these heads at the base rate. Zeroing them never reproduces abliteration's refusal collapse, so detection is separable from execution. They add that the joint head output encodes register rather than harm category at their readout position. The refusal-collapse comparison point is asserted, not measured.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than directly extracting and ablating or adding a residual-stream difference-in-means direction, the study selects heads with a harmful-versus-benign specificity score, compares base/instruct/abliterated checkpoints, and zero-ablates selected head sets. The tested abliterated checkpoints are public community releases.
record.method_sensitivity: The recruitment-direction result varies across checkpoint set and abliterated recipe; it is null on some model sets. The detection probe declines after abliteration on Gemma-3-4B but not Qwen3-8B. Ablation effects vary by head set and prompt condition; the both-set result is near zero while the Gemma-3-4B retained set raises compliance.

fits_no_version.finding: Different abliteration recipes on Gemma-3-4B erase different head sets. Diff-in-means recipes agree with each other (Jaccard 0.69–0.79), but per-layer directions erase a chance-overlapping set. A KL-constrained optimizer (Heretic) is said to remove refusal while lowering no head's S3 (direction p=1.0).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Which attention heads lose harm specificity under refusal removal depends on the removal recipe, consistent with a non-unique refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Seeded NMF over detection-head outputs organizes prompts by register and source dataset, not harm category. Harm-category alignment appears only at the post-chat-template readout position.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: What safety-selected heads encode depends on readout position and is dominated by prompt register.

record.problems: The main compliance judge is an LLM panel and the authors acknowledge judge biases. The qualitative refusal-collapse claim for the released abliterated models has no refusal-rate or uncertainty figures in the cited discussion. The paper states that its linear detection read-off is distribution-narrow and does not support deployment at a fixed threshold. Several findings depend on head selection and checkpoint/abliteration recipe.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcome rows left out. The paper's direction-test p-values and head-count provenance results concern the specificity-score-selected heads, not direct measurement or intervention on the original single residual-stream refusal direction.

untested.parts: The study never extracts, projects out or adds the difference-in-means direction itself, and does not check capability preservation. Abliterated checkpoints are third-party releases, apart from two in-house diff-in-means abliterations used only for head-set scoring.
No refusal rates or capability effects are measured for any abliterated checkpoint. That abliteration removes refusal is assumed or asserted, not shown.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction, or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
No direct test of affine, cone or multi-direction accounts. Recipe-dependent erased head sets are noted as consistent with a non-unique direction, but no refusal measure is tied to that.
No transfer of the direction across languages, variants, or base to instruct.
Training method or timing is not varied; the base, instruct and abliterated comparison is about head specificity, not refusal-direction existence.
Reasoning models are not studied as such. Qwen3 think blocks are noted only as a truncation issue.

missing.what: Circularity control: refusal-direction alignment explains under 6% of heads' instruct-minus-abliterated S3 variance (Qwen R²=0.040, p=0.33; Gemma R²=0.058, p=0.06). This is evidence that the detection heads are not aligned with the refusal direction.
Zeroing the 19 heads selected only by the unsafe-only score cuts Gemma-3-4B's harmful-prompt first-token refusal mass from 0.50 to 0.05 (Holm p=0.03). Non-specific heads do carry refusal execution.
Zeroing the both sets moves first-token refusal mass no more than 20 random matched draws (p≥0.24).
Gemma-3-4B detection AUROC of the 36 both heads under six abliteration recipes: 0.810–0.912, against 0.965 at instruct.
Gemma-3-4B dose ladder top rung k=59: judged compliance +10.1 pp (Holm p=4e-6), with the marker scorer not significant after correction and mild fluency loss.

On Gemma-4-31B, the worst-case alignment between a taxonomy component and the refusal direction is 0.1023 at the scaffold position and 0.1506 post-chat-template, breaching the 0.1 bar. The detection–execution geometry is position-qualified at scale.

record.verdict_notes: V2 rows were reset to cannot_determine: the paper never measures refusal on the abliterated checkpoints, and its contrast with 'refusal collapse' rests on that unmeasured assertion. V5 row states were reframed against V5, so null compliance change counts as observed separation. The detection construct is head-level S3 and a linear probe on head outputs, not the harmfulness residual direction of Zhao et al. Compliance is scored by an LLM judge panel with N=200–400.

versions.untested_parts: Does not directly extract, project out, or add the difference-in-means residual direction, or test the stated broad capability preservation.
Does not report refusal rates or capability effects numerically for the released abliterated checkpoints; the refusal-collapse result is stated qualitatively.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation increases robustness.
Does not directly compare single-direction, affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
Tests selected head-set ablations and probe-readable harmful-versus-safe separation, not a complete causal account of the harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Cross-checkpoint detection-head results are not a test of transfer of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Compares base, instruct, and abliterated checkpoints, but does not vary refusal-training method or timing.
Does not test reasoning models as a distinct setting.

relationships.condition: Zero-ablating the 'both' detection head sets (recruited by fine-tuning and erased by abliteration) on AILuminate, jailbreak-wrapped and borderline prompts in Qwen3-8B, Gemma-3-4B and Gemma-4-E4B. Also Qwen3-8B's retained set, and the probe after abliteration on Qwen3-8B.
relationships.reason: Judged compliance is unchanged within ±5 pp after zeroing detection heads (r5, r6, r7, r9, r10, r11). On Qwen3-8B the detection probe survives abliteration, AUROC 0.875 to 0.886 (r3). Detection is head-level here, not a residual direction.
relationships.display_finding: Detection-head ablation changed compliance by no more than ±5 percentage points, while Qwen3-8B detection-probe AUROC changed from 0.875 to 0.886 after abliteration.

relationships.condition: Gemma-3-4B: detection probe after abliteration, and ablation of the retained head set
relationships.reason: On Gemma-3-4B, abliteration degrades detection, AUROC 0.965 to 0.875 (0.81–0.91 across six recipes, per the text) (r4). Zeroing its 23 retained detection heads raises compliance +5.6 pp (r8), so detection and execution are partly coupled on this model.
relationships.display_finding: Abliteration reduced detection AUROC from 0.965 to 0.875, ranging from 0.81–0.91 across six recipes, while ablating 23 retained detection heads increased compliance by 5.6 percentage points.

relation.reason: Zero-ablation of detection heads with judged compliance, and probes read after abliteration, bear directly on whether harm detection is separate from refusal (V5).

tranche.reason: The study's own results test V5 with a different method: head-level S3 selection, zero-ablation, and probing on abliterated checkpoints. The results mostly support V5, with partial coupling on Gemma-3-4B. Its critique of the single-direction account is framing. It reports no refusal-direction ablation results or abliterated refusal rates showing that V1 is wrong.

source_check.notes: The pack listed verdicts without [lN] ids, so l1 and l2 follow the listed order. Abliterated checkpoints are mostly community (huihui-ai) releases, and no refusal rates are reported for them. Base probes (0.74-0.80) fall below an input-only text classifier (0.979 Alpaca contrast, 0.852 harm-matched), so surviving AUROC may partly reflect text separability. Results not among the checked rows: Gemma-3-4B k=59 rung +10.1 pp; Qwen3.5-4B mid-dose +6.09 pp (Table 3). Under review at ICLR 2027. The per-page ICLR reviewer footer is standard template text, not an injection.

statements.correction: Gemma-3-4B both-36 set: jailbreak-wrapped +0.5 pp, 90% CI [-2.5, +3.5]; borderline-benign +1.0 pp, 90% CI [-2.5, +4.6]; 200-700 prompts per cell. Text says no primary cell rises (Holm p = 1.0) but gives no Qwen pool numbers. Both sets zeroed: Qwen3-8B 16 heads, Gemma-3-4B 36, Gemma-4-E4B 10. Qwen CI is 95%.
statements.problem: The jailbreak-wrapped (+0.5 pp) and borderline (+1.0 pp) numbers are for Gemma-3-4B only, but the statement gives them no model after listing three. The zeroed set is the 'both' set (recruited and erased), not every head that abliteration erases.

statements.correction: Qwen3-8B abliterated checkpoint: huihui-ai community release (Appendix G). Only two of the six Gemma-3-4B abliterations (D1 AdvBench, D2 StrongREJECT) are in-house. Gemma-3-4B both-36 AUROC: 0.965 instruct -> 0.810-0.912 across the six. Qwen3-8B 16 both heads: 0.875 -> 0.886.
statements.problem: The conditions say Qwen3-8B was abliterated by 2eoMtzq03h. The paper says every main abliterated checkpoint is a public huihui-ai community release. The six Gemma-3-4B recipes cited in 'why' show a decline, not harm staying decodable at the instruct level.

statements.correction: Gemma-3-4B abliterations: huihui-ai 0.875, mlabonne v2 0.855, Heretic 0.837, mlabonne v1 0.810 (all public), in-house D1 0.912, D2 0.883 (Table 9). The claim that abliteration 'breaks refusal outright' is asserted, with no rates given.
statements.problem: 'Six recipes applied by 2eoMtzq03h' is wrong: four of the six are public releases and two are in-house. The 0.875 headline itself comes from the huihui-ai community checkpoint. The study reports no measured refusal rate for any abliterated checkpoint, so the community/unverified difference does not separate the two studies.

statements.correction: Both sets: 0.0, -0.3 and 0.0 pp, equivalent within ±5 pp. Gemma-3-4B 23 retained heads: +5.6 pp [+2.3, +8.9]. Gemma-3-4B dose rung k=59: +10.1 pp (Holm p = 4e-6). Authors: zeroing moves compliance 'by at most ten points'.
statements.problem: 'Within about ±5 pp' holds only for the zeroed 'both' sets. Other detection-selected sets on Gemma-3-4B move more.

statements.correction: Both-set zeroing: Qwen3-8B 0.0 pp [-5.2, +5.2]; Gemma-3-4B -0.3 pp; Gemma-4-E4B 0.0 pp. Gemma-3-4B retained set: +5.6 pp.
statements.problem: Minor: the 0.0 pp is for the both sets on Qwen3-8B and Gemma-4-E4B (Gemma-3-4B: -0.3 pp). Gemma-4-E4B is 4B effective, outside '7-9B'.
